utility.notes: Gonzales is a well-documented Monterey County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

value.name: Central Coast Community Energy (3CE)
value.notes: 3CE's own official site confirms it serves Monterey County, and separately lists Gonzales among its named member communities. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

permit_url.notes: The city has an expedited permitting process for small residential rooftop solar with a published eligibility checklist (per search-engine summary), but the fetched page did not itself surface that checklist's content.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Gonzales/Monterey County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value: Schedule via the Online Permitting Portal, or by calling (831) 675-5000
Building inspections are conducted Tuesdays and Thursdays, 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM, unless other arrangements are made with the Building Inspector in advance
When scheduling, provide the building permit number and address, date/time requested, type of inspection, and contact information for the person on-site (must be 18+ or the responsible contractor)
The building permit card and official City-stamped approved plans must be on-site at all times
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.notes: General new-residential-construction review can take up to 30 days to complete; a separate expedited timeline specific to small rooftop solar was not confirmed this session.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited permitting process for small residential rooftop solar energy systems
other_conditions: Electronic submittal of applications and documentation is accepted, with electronic signatures accepted in lieu of wet signatures
